Gastrointestinal Anthrax Preferred Regimens: Regimen 1: Administer ciprofloxacin 400 mg intravenously (IV) every 8 hours (q8h) in combination with clindamycin 600 mg IV q8h. Regimen 2: Administer ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h in combination with penicillin G 4 million units (MU) every 4–6 hours. Regimen 3: Administer ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h in combination with meropenem 1 g IV every 6–8 hours. Regimen 4: Administer ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h in combination with rifampin 300 mg every 12 hours (q12h). Regimen 5: Administer doxycycline 100 mg IV q12h in combination with clindamycin 600 mg IV q8h. Regimen 6: Administer doxycycline 100 mg IV q12h in combination with penicillin G 4 MU every 4–6 hours. Regimen 7: Administer doxycycline 100 mg IV q12h in combination with meropenem 1 g IV every 6–8 hours. Regimen 8: Administer doxycycline 100 mg IV q12h in combination with rifampin 300 mg q12h. Note: Treatment should continue for 60 days to prevent relapse or breakthrough of incubating disease. If initial therapy is IV, transition to oral administration (ciprofloxacin or doxycycline) when clinically appropriate. Steroids may be considered as adjunct therapy for patients with severe edema or meningitis. For pregnant women, avoid doxycycline; instead, use ciprofloxacin and switch to oral penicillin once susceptibilities are confirmed. Appendicitis 1. Combination Therapy Preferred Regimens: Regimen 1: Cefepime 2 g IV every 8–12 hours in combination with metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h or 1500 mg IV q24h. Regimen 2: Ceftazidime 2 g IV q8h in combination with metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h or 1500 mg IV q24h. Regimen 3: Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h in combination with metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h or 1500 mg IV q24h. Regimen 4: Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h in combination with metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h or 1500 mg IV q24h. Note: Antimicrobial therapy for established infection should be limited to 4–7 days unless achieving adequate source control is challenging. Longer durations of therapy have not been associated with improved outcomes. 2. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA): Preferred Regimen: Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV q8–12h. Note: Antimicrobial therapy for established infection should be limited to 4–7 days unless achieving adequate source control is challenging. Alternative Regimens: Caspofungin 50 mg IV daily after a 70 mg loading dose. Micafungin 150 mg IV daily. Anidulafungin 50 mg IV daily after a 100 mg loading dose. Note: Maintenance therapy with fluconazole 100–200 mg orally daily is recommended for AIDS patients. 2. Herpes Simplex Virus Esophagitis: Preferred Regimens: Acyclovir 5 mg/kg IV q8h for 7–14 days. Acyclovir 400 mg orally five times daily for 14–21 days. Valacyclovir 1 g orally three times daily for 14–21 days. Alternative Regimens: Famciclovir 500 mg orally twice daily for 14–21 days.
